title: Elastic Reserve Negotiator & Isolation Grace Policies (PRD)
creator: Sofia Chen
description: Introduce an Elastic Reservation Negotiator coupled with Isolation Grace policies to reduce customer-visible throttles and improve utilization. The Negotiator allows tenants to request short-term elastic credits that can be granted, queued, or partially accepted based on global headroom, fairness constraints, and tenant priority. Isolation Grace enforces a time-bounded soft-fencing window and gentle preemption semantics (soft-evict) to avoid hard failures during transient bursts.
scope: In scope: API (reservation negotiation endpoints), scheduler changes to accept temporary credits, new quota ledger for elastic credits, console UX to request and view negotiations, telemetry for credit grants/denials, and rollout tooling for canary-enabled tenants. Out of scope: major cluster autoscaler rework, on-prem installation changes requiring offline upgrades, and billing contract negotiation workflows (handled by sales).
requirements: R1: New REST endpoint POST /v1/dedicated/reservation/negotiate to request elastic credit with fields {tenant_id, duration_seconds, requested_rps, priority_hint, fallback_policy}
R2: Scheduler accepts negotiation decisions (grant/partial/granular-queue/deny) and emits decision events to ledger and audit log within 5s of request under normal load
R3: Credit ledger stores granted credit units with expiry timestamps and supports idempotent renew and revoke
R4: Isolation Grace: implement soft-fencing window param per tenant (default 30s) where requests can be served with degraded QoS before hard-preemption
R5: Fairness policy: negotiator must respect tenant share windows and not reduce any reserved tenant below their reserved baseline SLA
R6: Autoscale hysteresis: negotiator decisions should include guidance for pre-warm when repeated requests exceed threshold for a tenant (configurable threshold: default 3 bump events within 2m)
R7: Console: allow tenant owners to request one-off elastic credits, view current credits, and simulate worst-case fallback impact
R8: Telemetry: dashboard showing granted vs requested credits, denial reasons, average decision latency, and tenant-level credit burn rate
R9: Access control: negotiation endpoint requires tenant-scoped key and records actor identity in audit logs
R10: Compatibility: fallback policy must allow automatic routing to cheaper model variant (if configured) or queue semantics with TTL
acceptance_criteria: AC1: API: negotiation endpoint passes contract tests (idempotency, input validation) and demo script shows grant/partial/deny flows
AC2: Scheduler: end-to-end latency for decision pipeline <= 5s P95 under 10k concurrent negotiation requests simulated
AC3: Soft-fencing: during induced evictions in a staging cluster, tenants with Isolation Grace experience fewer hard failures; validated by <1 hard-preempt per 1000 requests vs baseline 5/1000
AC4: Fairness: experiments show no reserved tenant experiences >5% SLA degradation when negotiator grants elastic credits to others in same pool
AC5: Console: product owners can perform a negotiation request and see accurate credit state and expiry in the UI within 10s of grant
AC6: Telemetry: dashboards populate within 60s of first decision and include breakdown by grant reason and denial reason
AC7: Security: audit logs include actor, tenant_id, decision_id and are stored in customer-managed KMS when Private mode is enabled
AC8: Rollout: feature can be toggled per-tenant; initial canary with 5 pilot tenants shows no regressions for 72h
success_metrics: SM1: Reduction in customer-visible throttling from transient bursts by >= 40% within first month of rollout
SM2: Increase in usable cluster utilization by 6-10% by safely packing elastic credits
SM3: Mean decision latency of negotiator pipeline < 2s after optimizations
SM4: < 0.1% incidents attributed to negotiation decision bugs during 30-day post-launch
rollout_plan: Step 0: Integration tests and contract tests merge (backend + ledger + console mocks)
Step 1: Deploy negotiator in staging; run load tests and chaos scenarios (evictions, delayed kernel selection)
Step 2: Enable feature flag for 5 pilot tenants for 72h; monitor SLA, errors, and metrics; collect feedback
Step 3: Expand to 50 tenants; run cost/regression analysis; tune fairness parameters
Step 4: Gradual global rollout to all dedicated pools over 2 weeks with automatic rollback on error budget breach
Step 5: Post-launch 30-day review and adjustments to default grace windows and pre-warm thresholds
metrics_and_dashboards: MD3: Tenant credit burn rate and expiry histogram
MD4: Hard-preempt vs soft-serve counts per tenant
MD5: Cluster headroom utilization and effective reserved baseline occupancy
security_and_compliance_notes: Audit log entries for negotiation decisions must be forwarded to customer KMS for Private deployments
Negotiation endpoint must enforce tenant-scoped auth tokens and rate limits (to prevent credit spam)
Privacy: do not include raw prompt texts in negotiation logs; only include tenant_id, request meta and decision reason
api_contract_examples: Idempotency: clients can provide client_request_id to dedupe repeated negotiation attempts
test_plan: Unit tests for negotiation grammar and validation
Integration tests: end-to-end with ledger and scheduler (simulate grants and revokes)
Load tests: 10k concurrent negotiation requests, measuring queueing and decision tail latency
Chaos tests: simulate node preemption while credits active; validate soft-fencing behavior
Security tests: ensure audit logs redact PII and respect KMS configuration
notes_and_open_questions: Q1: How should credit cost be billed in mixed-mode (hosted + dedicated) tenants? Need finance input
Q2: Do we auto-replenish credits for long-lived spikes? Proposal: no auto-replenish, require explicit renew to avoid runaway charges
Q3: Default isolation grace window set to 30s; ops may want per-pool tuning for noisy neighbors
Q4: Interaction with existing preemptive credit pools needs coordination with capacity team (ENG-28901)
